title: AWS CWI Training in San Antonio, TX: 6-Day Exam Prep
description: Six-day AWS CWI exam prep for San Antonio aerospace MRO, automotive, data center and pipeline welders. Corporate, online or one-to-one formats.
h1: AWS CWI Exam Prep in San Antonio: Six Days for Aerospace, Automotive and Construction Welding Inspectors
html:
San Antonio welds a little of everything. Engine shops and hangars at Port San Antonio repair military and commercial aircraft, the Toyota truck plant on the South Side is adding a second assembly line, data center campuses are rising on the West Side, and pipeline crews still work the Eagle Ford Shale to the south and east. Each of those employers needs someone who can check a weld against a written standard and sign the record. Atlantis NDT prepares people for the American Welding Society's Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) examination with a six-day (6-day) course. It comes in three formats: corporate delivery at an employer's facility, online self-paced study with an instructor answering questions, and one-to-one sessions online or in person. AWS administers the examination and issues the certification, while preparation is the whole of what Atlantis does. There is no Atlantis classroom in San Antonio, and the course has no AWS approval, accreditation or endorsement. To scope it for yourself or a crew, send a San Antonio CWI exam prep enquiry.

How do the six days work for a San Antonio candidate?

All three formats follow one outline. Days one and two build the Part A Fundamentals: welding processes, AWS A3.0 terms, joint design, A2.4 symbols, metallurgy, mechanical and nondestructive testing, discontinuities, safety and inspection math. Day three rehearses the Part B practical with gauges, specimens and procedure documents. Day four is spent inside the code book you will open in Part C. Day five is timed practice papers, and day six goes back over weak areas and exam logistics. Each day is broken down on the national AWS CWI exam prep page.

  • Corporate. A San Antonio employer with several people to prepare hosts all six days at its own shop, hangar or plant. The group practises on the company's welds and gauges and, where it fits, its own code and procedures.
  • Online. An individual gets a study plan built on the six-day outline, the course materials, original practice questions and timed practice papers, and sends questions to an instructor while working through them. Nothing is scheduled; you set the pace around your shifts.
  • One-to-one. A single candidate books six days of one-to-one sessions with the instructor, either online or in person at a location agreed when booking. This suits someone with a fixed exam date and a particular gap, such as code navigation or symbol reading.

Every practice question is written by Atlantis to the subject areas AWS publishes. No question is copied from the AWS examination, and Atlantis has no access to AWS question banks or to anyone's scores.

Where San Antonio welds get inspected

Aircraft maintenance and engine repair at Port San Antonio

The former Kelly Air Force Base is now Port San Antonio, an industrial and aerospace campus built around the Kelly Field runway. The Port lists Boeing, which operates very large hangars there; StandardAero, which overhauls commercial and military engines; Chromalloy, which repairs engine components such as cases, frames, shafts and disks; and Knight Aerospace, which builds quick-change medical modules for cargo aircraft. AWS itself describes the city as a national hub for aircraft maintenance, repair and overhaul. Welding in that world is precise, small-scale and heavily documented: gas tungsten arc repairs on nickel and titanium alloys, brackets and ducts, tooling and ground support equipment. Inspection is about weld class, acceptance limits, traceability and paperwork rather than big fillet welds.

Toyota Texas and the on-site supplier park

Toyota's San Antonio plant is the exclusive home of the Tundra and Sequoia, and in July 2026 Toyota announced a second assembly line on the same campus, with Tacoma production moving there from Baja California over roughly four years and a new rear axle facility starting up. Toyota says its local workforce is supported by 23 on-site suppliers. Automotive production welding is mostly robotic and is judged against the automaker's and suppliers' own weld standards rather than an AWS structural code. A CWI in that setting usually owns the welding quality system: procedure control, operator qualification, destructive checks on production samples and visual audit. The expansion itself is a large structural steel job, and that work falls under AWS D1.1.

Data centers and plant construction on the West Side

Microsoft has posted construction updates for several San Antonio data center sites, including Westover Link, where its general contractor Walbridge began site clearing and excavation. Data halls, substations and the steel frames that carry heavy mechanical systems keep structural erectors and testing agencies busy. On those jobs a welding inspector checks welder qualification records, joint preparation, fillet size and profile, and writes the reports the owner and building official read. Long summer days in South Texas heat add their own risk: electrodes left out of rod ovens, coatings applied to hot steel, and tired welders on overhead joints.

Pipelines and gathering systems in the Eagle Ford

The Eagle Ford Shale spreads across counties south and east of the city, and San Antonio is a natural base for the crews that build and repair its gathering lines, compressor stations and transmission tie-ins. Pipeline construction specifications normally call up API 1104 for welding procedures, welder qualification and weld acceptance. Inspectors on those spreads spend long stretches on the road, so a self-paced format matters more to them than to anyone else in the city.

Military construction and base maintenance

AWS calls San Antonio "Military City USA", and Joint Base San Antonio brings a steady flow of hangar, utility and building work. Federal construction specifications usually reference AWS D1.1 for structural steel and expect documented inspection by qualified personnel. Contractors bidding that work often need a CWI on the quality control plan before the first beam arrives.

Who hires CWIs around San Antonio, and what do they ask for?

  • Aerospace MRO and component repair shops want inspectors who can read a customer specification, keep records traceable to the part and work comfortably with very small welds. A CWI shows broad welding knowledge; the shop then trains you on its own procedures.
  • Automotive suppliers look for people who can run a weld-quality program, train operators, investigate defects and talk to the customer's supplier quality engineers.
  • Structural fabricators, erectors and testing agencies need D1.1 inspectors for data centers, plant expansions, hospitals and military buildings, both in the shop and in the field.
  • Pipeline contractors and operators staff API 1104 inspectors for new lines, tie-ins and integrity repairs, mostly on the road.
  • Owner and engineering firms hire CWIs to review contractors' welding documents and audit fabricators before steel ships.

Pay depends on the code you know, travel and overtime as much as on the credential. For context on how the CWI compares with other routes, read CWI requirements and career impact.

Which Part C code fits San Antonio work?

Part C is open book, and you choose the book when you apply. The AWS list covers D1.1 for structural steel, API 1104 for pipelines, D1.2 for aluminum structures, D1.5 for bridges, D15.1 for railcars and locomotives, D17.1 for aerospace fusion welding, an ASME package that pairs Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3, and an ISO option. In San Antonio the choice usually comes down to four.

If your San Antonio work is mostlyConsiderWhy
Aircraft, engine or component repair at Port San Antonio or a supplierAWS D17.1It organizes aerospace fusion welds by class, with inspection and acceptance criteria per class
Data centers, plant expansions, military buildings, structural fabricationAWS D1.1Prequalified joints, qualification, fabrication tolerances and visual acceptance for structural steel
Eagle Ford gathering, transmission and station workAPI 1104Procedure and welder qualification by destructive testing, and field acceptance standards
Power plant or process piping, including utility and chilled water plants built to ASME codesASME Section IX with B31.1 and B31.3Qualification variables and piping examination rules

Automotive production welding has no book of its own on the list. Candidates from supplier plants usually pick D1.1, because plant structures, fixtures and tooling bases follow it and its logic transfers well. Study the edition AWS names for the exam, which can lag the newest printing. Background reading: AWS D1.1, API 1104 and AWS D1.5.

The AWS San Antonio Section and the local welding pipeline

San Antonio has its own AWS section, part of District 18. Its recent calendar has included section meetings at a local vocational school campus and a facility tour of the Palo Alto College welding shop, held alongside a bylaws vote. Section meetings are where a CWI candidate meets working inspectors, finds people who can confirm welding history for the AWS application, and hears which employers are hiring. Contact details and the calendar are on the section's pages at sections.aws.org.

Most inspectors start out as welders, and in San Antonio the Alamo Colleges are an obvious place to learn the trade. Palo Alto College roughly doubled its welding shop in 2025, adding booths to meet demand, and the district is planning a Center of Applied Technology at Brooks under its 2025 bond. St. Philip's College, another Alamo College, also runs a welding technology program. A college record helps in two ways: AWS lets relevant education reduce the work experience it asks for, and school transcripts are easier to document than years of informal shop work. These colleges are named here as part of the local pipeline; they are not Atlantis partners or venues.

Booking the exam from San Antonio

Once AWS accepts your application, its confirmation letter carries the eligibility code Prometric asks for. With it you reserve seats for the two computer-based parts: Part A, 150 Fundamentals questions, and Part C, roughly 50 to 65 questions in your chosen code with the book open. AWS reports more than 100 Prometric centers in the United States; Prometric's own site shows the ones nearest your ZIP code.

Part B is different. AWS runs the practical itself, combining hands-on tasks with AWS-supplied tools and specimens and 46 written questions, at its own seminar and exam locations. AWS publishes a CWI location page for San Antonio, but when we checked it in November 2026 it showed no upcoming Texas seminars, so look at the AWS seminar and exam schedule early and be ready to drive to Houston, Austin or another city if that is where a session falls. AWS requires at least 72% on each part, and it publishes its examination fees on aws.org. For a full budget including travel and the code book, use the CWI exam cost planner.

Studying around production shifts, hangar schedules and summer heat

San Antonio's employers keep very different hours. An automotive supplier runs fixed production shifts with planned shutdown weeks, an engine shop works to aircraft induction and delivery dates, a structural crew starts before dawn in July to beat the heat, and a pipeline inspector may be two hours down a lease road for weeks. The online format is designed for that spread: work through Fundamentals during a quieter month, keep the code book in the truck or locker and look up the clauses that apply to the joints you see that week, and save the timed papers for the fortnight before your Prometric date.

A practical habit for Part B is to measure every weld you can reach. Fillet legs, convexity, undercut depth and misalignment are skills of the hand and eye, and San Antonio shops throw away plenty of coupons and cut-outs to practise on. Write the number down before you judge it. The Practical NDT welding workshop simulator lets you rehearse inspection steps in a browser between shifts.

Corporate: six days at a San Antonio-area employer's facility

For a company preparing a group, the corporate format brings the full outline to its own floor. A Port San Antonio repair shop might split the code day between D17.1 for its welders and D1.1 for its facilities and tooling staff. A structural fabricator supplying data center steel can run every exercise in D1.1, using its own weld maps and shop drawings. An automotive supplier may want the practical day built around its production samples, so the measurement work matches the parts its people sign off.

The practical day uses the employer's fillet gauges, bridge cam gauges, undercut gauges and hi-lo gauges on real welds, including welder test plates and rejected parts. Timing is agreed around production, shutdowns or aircraft deliveries. Each person still applies to AWS individually and must meet the education, experience and vision rules personally; an employer cannot apply on anyone's behalf.

One-to-one sessions for a single San Antonio candidate

Booked one-to-one, the six days become private sessions between you and the instructor. Online sessions work well for someone whose shifts rotate or who travels to the Eagle Ford. In-person sessions happen at a location agreed when you book, which might be the candidate's workplace or another suitable room; there is still no Atlantis classroom in the city. One-to-one is often the right choice for a candidate who has failed one part and needs focused work on it, such as Part C navigation in D17.1 or the inspection math in Part A. For a sense of where candidates tend to struggle, read CWI results by exam part.

Eligibility and the vision record

AWS sets the experience requirement by education. A high school diploma means five years of welding-related work; an associate degree in an engineering technology, engineering or physical science field means two; a bachelor's in welding engineering or welding technology means one. Whether a particular college program counts toward a shorter route is AWS's call, not the college's or Atlantis's. Vision is recorded on the AWS Visual Acuity Record: near vision of Jaeger J2 at 12 inches or more, with or without glasses, plus color perception, done by a qualified practitioner within the time AWS allows before your exam. Candidates short of the experience can look at the Certified Associate Welding Inspector (CAWI) first. The full table is on the national CWI course page.

People leaving service at Joint Base San Antonio often bring aircraft maintenance, structural repair or welding experience. Whether that history counts toward the CWI is AWS's decision, so document duties, dates and supervisors carefully. The guide to veterans transitioning into NDT covers related routes.

After the CWI: career paths in San Antonio

AWS keeps the CWI valid for nine years, with renewal filings due at the third and sixth years and recertification at nine. Locally the next step tends to follow the sector:

  • Aerospace inspectors often add nondestructive testing so they can run penetrant, magnetic particle or ultrasonic checks on repaired parts themselves. Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A the employer certifies NDT staff once training and method hours are in place; Atlantis provides that training. See aviation NDT training in San Antonio and penetrant testing in aviation.
  • Structural and construction inspectors build toward the Senior CWI (SCWI) and AWS endorsements; see the Senior CWI pathway.
  • Visual inspection depth through VT Level 2 training strengthens the core skill of the CWI; see also visual testing and weld inspection.
  • Weighing credentials: the side-by-side of AWS CWI, API 577 and ASNT Level II explains what each certifies and who issues it.

For local NDT courses, see NDT training in San Antonio, and for local inspection work, ultrasonic testing in San Antonio, magnetic particle testing in San Antonio and the Practical NDT simulator for San Antonio.

Other Texas CWI pages and requesting a quote

Candidates elsewhere in the state can read the CWI exam prep pages for Houston, Dallas, Fort Worth, Corpus Christi and Beaumont.

For a quote, tell us which format you want (corporate, online or one-to-one), how many candidates, each person's schooling and welding history in outline, and the Part C book each plans to choose. For corporate delivery, add the facility location, the gauges and sample welds on hand and the weeks that suit production. Use the San Antonio CWI enquiry form. AWS publishes its own exam fees; the course is quoted on request.

faq.q: Is there an Atlantis CWI classroom in San Antonio?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in San Antonio. You can study online at your own pace with an instructor answering questions, book six days of one-to-one sessions online or in person at an agreed location, or have an employer host the six days at its own facility. See the course outline.

faq.q: Does finishing the six days make me a CWI in Texas?
faq.a: No. AWS reviews your application, runs all three parts of the examination and issues the certification to candidates who pass. Atlantis prepares candidates and certifies no one, and AWS has not approved or endorsed the course.

faq.q: I repair engine parts at Port San Antonio. Which Part C code should I choose?
faq.a: Many aerospace candidates choose AWS D17.1, the aerospace fusion welding specification, because it organizes welds by class with matching inspection and acceptance criteria. If your role is mostly facilities, tooling or structural work, D1.1 may suit you better.

faq.q: Which code suits data center or plant construction work in San Antonio?
faq.a: AWS D1.1, the structural steel code that construction specifications for data halls, plant expansions and military buildings normally call up. See AWS D1.1.

faq.q: Where do San Antonio candidates take the CWI exam?
faq.a: Parts A and C are computer-based tests booked with Prometric using the eligibility code in your AWS confirmation letter. Part B is run by AWS at its own seminar locations; AWS has a San Antonio location page, but in November 2026 it showed no upcoming Texas seminars, so check the schedule early and plan for travel.

faq.q: Should I choose online or in-person one-to-one sessions?
faq.a: Online sessions suit rotating shifts and pipeline travel. In-person sessions take place at a location agreed when you book. Both give you six days of one-to-one time with the instructor; the choice is about convenience, not content.

faq.q: Can a Toyota supplier or structural fabricator have the course run at its plant?
faq.a: Yes. The corporate format brings all six days to your facility, uses your gauges and production welds, and can split the code day if people need different books. Each candidate still applies to AWS individually. Request a quote.

faq.q: Are the practice questions taken from the AWS exam?
faq.a: No. Atlantis writes every practice question and timed paper to the subject areas AWS publishes. It has no access to the AWS examination or its question bank.

faq.q: Does military welding or aircraft maintenance experience count toward the CWI?
faq.a: AWS decides what counts as qualifying welding-related experience. Document your duties, dates and supervisors so AWS can verify them. See veterans transitioning into NDT for related routes.

faq.q: Does Atlantis offer NDT training in San Antonio too?
faq.a: Yes. Atlantis provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training in VT, MT, PT and UT, and the employer certifies its staff under its written practice. See NDT training in San Antonio and aviation NDT training.
